title: LIBRA: Measuring Bias of Large Language Model from a Local Context

bias_targets.methodology: Constructing localized triplet datasets (stereotyped, anti-stereotyped, irrelevant) from regional corpora (e.g., New Zealand, Malaysia) without crowdsourcing, and computing the Enhanced Idealized CAT Score (EiCAT) which integrates the Jensen-Shannon Divergence of choice logits with a 'beyond knowledge boundary score' (bbs).

Measuring the Jensen-Shannon Divergence between the probability distributions of stereotyped and anti-stereotyped choice logits using a localized triplet dataset derived from New Zealand corpora, where age-related content makes up 73.43% of the dataset.
Evaluating model logits on stereotyped versus anti-stereotyped sentences associated with gender groups, extracted from local New Zealand media corpora.
Analyzing probability distributions of model logits on sentence triplets targeting racial and ethnic groups (including indigenous Māori populations) using context-specific New Zealand terminology.
Evaluating model logits on stereotyped versus anti-stereotyped sentences associated with sexual orientation, extracted from local New Zealand media corpora.
Evaluating model logits on stereotyped versus anti-stereotyped sentences associated with physical appearance, extracted from local New Zealand media corpora.
Evaluating model logits on stereotyped versus anti-stereotyped sentences associated with disability status, identified via seed keywords and association rule learning within local corpora.
Evaluating model logits on stereotyped versus anti-stereotyped sentences associated with nationalities, extracted from local New Zealand media corpora.
Evaluating model logits on stereotyped versus anti-stereotyped sentences associated with religion, extracted from local New Zealand media corpora.
